name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area GDP grew 0.4% in Q3, confirmed on 13 Nov; October composite PMI 51.7; November flash PMIs due 23 Nov
state: Eurostat's second estimate on 13 Nov left euro-area third-quarter GDP growth at 0.4% on the quarter, unchanged from the flash (Eurostat; investingLive). The HCOB composite PMI was 51.7 in October, a four-month low but above 50. November flash PMIs had not been published as of 22 Nov and are due on 23 Nov, so the latest data remain consistent with Normal.
for_you: Euro-area activity is still growing slowly. Exporters and firms exporting to Europe face steady but soft demand; the 23 Nov PMI figures will show whether that held into November.

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
investingLive — Eurozone Q3 GDP unchanged in second estimate as uneven growth clouds the outlook

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
